name: Thinning Hair
description: Thinning hair, also known as hair miniaturization or female pattern baldness in women, is a condition where the diameter of individual hair follicles decreases over time. This results in finer and shorter hair growth, leading to a noticeable thinning of the scalp's hair density.
causes: Hormonal Changes (such as menopause or thyroid disorders)
Medications (like chemotherapy drugs, blood thinners, or antidepressants)
symptoms: Hair becoming finer and lighter in texture
Hair thinning on the top of the scalp

daily_routine.step: Gentle cleansing with a mild shampoo.
daily_routine.purpose: To remove dirt, oil, and product build-up without stripping the scalp.

daily_routine.step: Application of a nourishing conditioner or serum.
daily_routine.purpose: To hydrate and strengthen hair strands.

daily_routine.step: Regular use of a leave-in conditioner or moisturizer.
daily_routine.purpose: To help retain moisture and improve hair's overall health.

natural_remedies: Egg yolk and honey hair mask
lifestyle_tips: Maintain a balanced diet rich in vitamins and minerals.
Avoid excessive heat styling tools on your hair.
Regular scalp massaging to improve blood circulation.
common_myths: Hair thinning is solely due to aging.
Using shampoo more frequently will clean the scalp better and stop hair loss.
when_to_consult_doctor: If hair thinning occurs suddenly, if there are accompanying symptoms like itching or pain, or if it significantly impacts your quality of life.
prevention: Manage stress through relaxation techniques such as meditation or yoga.
Eat a balanced diet rich in proteins and vitamins.
Avoid harsh chemical treatments on your hair.

severity_levels.mild: Visible thinning but no bald patches, mild to moderate hair loss.
severity_levels.moderate: More noticeable thinning with some visible bald patches, moderate hair loss.
severity_levels.severe: Severe thinning or baldness, significant hair loss.

expert_tips: Consult a dermatologist for personalized treatment plans and assessments.
Be patient; results from treatments may take several months to show.
